clue.text: Multinational capital rolled into football club

indicators.note: into means the word for rolled is placed inside the club's letters

parts.note: rolled as in moved along, past tense of run gives ran

explanation.surface: Money from a big international firm gets poured into a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here is money, not a city: the franc has been the currency of several countries at once, from France and Switzerland to much of West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The franc is a currency used across many nations, such as the Swiss franc and the West African CFA franc.

clue.text: Dutch provincial, not available, is returning after one day

indicators.note: after means the reversed part comes after the day

parts.note: FRI is the abbreviation for Friday

indicators.note: returning means the letters are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone from a Dutch province is unavailable, coming back after a day away.
explanation.definitionFit: A Frisian is a native of Friesland, a province in the northern Netherlands.

clue.text: Sort out bits of grammar analysis in Our Mutual Friend

indicators.note: sort out means put in a fresh order, so the letters are rearranged
bits of means just the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: A student parses the grammar of Dickens's novel Our Mutual Friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for a friend, used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Some butter in tea bread

indicators.note: in means the butter goes inside the tea

parts.note: chai is tea, especially spiced Indian tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: A knob of butter is put in some tea bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread from South Asia.

clue.text: Attitudes on setter's burdens

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so the attitudes follow the setter's word

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, and setter's (setter is) gives I'M
poses are bodily attitudes or postures

explanation.surface: A setter's opinionated stances weigh heavily on others.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose is to lay a load or obligation on someone, so the verb matches burdens.

clue.text: With which flies can safely be undone in public?

definitions.text: With which flies can safely be undone in public?

parts.words: With which flies can safely be undone in public
parts.note: flies reads as a trouser zip, but the insects are what this substance undoes, or keeps away, out of doors

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at undoing trouser flies in public; the real flies are insects, kept off by a spray or cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A repellent applied to skin deters biting insects such as mosquitoes and midges outdoors.

clue.text: Mrs Grundy inspires Elgar's first two overtures? Just the one

indicators.note: inspires means breathes in, so the prude takes the letters inside

parts.note: Mrs Grundy is a byword for a narrow-minded prude
the first two letters of Elgar

explanation.surface: A prudish critic hears the opening two overtures of an Elgar concert, but sits through only one.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy is a character from an 18th-century play who stands for prudishness.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, a single overture.

clue.text: Aids those on bench, team checking one for inclusion

indicators.note: for inclusion means the substitutes take the team inside them

parts.note: subs are substitutes waiting on the bench

indicators.note: checking means holding in, so the team contains the one

parts.note: a side is a team
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Substitutes help the team keep an eye on one player being picked.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'checking' (holding in check) makes the team hold the one, and 'for inclusion' puts that inside the bench players.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsidies are grants of money that support an industry or service.

clue.text: Marshal notices division

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A marshal spots a division of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a military noun but is the verb to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a part or division of something.

clue.text: Northern Ireland with both sides in semi final? No

indicators.note: both sides means the two outer letters of the word semi are taken

explanation.surface: A Northern Ireland side reached the semi-final but not the final.
explanation.walkthrough: In English divorce law a decree nisi is provisional, not the final decree, hence 'final? No'.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree nisi takes effect only later unless cause is shown, so it is the stage that is not yet absolute.

clue.text: Sadly, 50% of "we care" banks respond impudently

indicators.note: sadly, as in badly or regrettably done, signals that the letters are muddled
half of the two-letter word we is its first letter

explanation.surface: A slogan about caring banks is greeted with cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' applies only to 'we', taking W; CARE and BANKS go into the anagram whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer back is to reply rudely or cheekily to someone in authority.

clue.text: Call to action intermittently set back female

indicators.note: set back means the letters chosen are written in reverse order
intermittently means taking every other letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A rallying call is postponed by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermittently' takes the alternate letters ALOCIN from 'Call to action', and 'set back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola is a woman's given name, so it is an example of a female.

clue.text: Perhaps third squad reportedly prepare for gymnastics exercise

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as they sound when spoken

parts.note: C is the third letter, so C crew is perhaps the third squad; C crew said aloud is crew-see
to fix a meal or drink is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A third-string team gets ready for a gymnastics routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'third squad' is C crew, as A, B and C crews; spoken, it gives the first part, and FIX (prepare) completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crucifix is a strength position on the rings with both arms spread out horizontally.

clue.text: Planning to get better inside, half of errant indigestion treated

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged
half of the six-letter word errant means its first three letters

explanation.surface: Someone plans to recover from a bout of indigestion with treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds medical but means making the inside of a room better.
explanation.definitionFit: The profession plans how rooms are decorated and furnished, improving a building's interior.

clue.text: Most immoderate texts, mere fragments

indicators.note: fragments, as a verb, means breaks into pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Wild extreme writings survive only as scraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremest is the superlative of extreme, the furthest from moderation.

clue.text: Article correct about media worker, say, supplying drug

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for correct is read backwards

parts.note: to edit a text is to correct it
the press is the news media
a worker ant is one kind of ant, so an ant is a worker, say

explanation.surface: A journalist's corrected article supplies some medication.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidepressant is a medication prescribed to lift depression.

clue.text: Property-transfer beneficiary originally called following a fabrication

indicators.note: following means the maiden-name word comes after the lie

parts.note: a lie is a fabrication
née, used before a maiden name, means born as or originally called

explanation.surface: A beneficiary of a property deal was given a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: An alienee is the person to whom property is legally conveyed, the receiver in a transfer.

clue.text: Not a time to sit in den — so busy

indicators.note: busy means bustling and active, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: The den is so busy there is no time to sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit' is what a court does: a dies non is a day on which no legal business is transacted.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies non is a legal term for a day when courts do not hold a session.

clue.text: Ranks Virginia, Georgia and a couple of Carolinas, for example

definitions.text: Virginia, Georgia and a couple of Carolinas, for example

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer as E STATES: Virginia, Georgia and both Carolinas lie along the US east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The estates are the social classes, such as clergy, nobility and commons; split, the word gives eastern states.

clue.text: Kings to avoid whisky? I'm afraid that's not possible

indicators.note: to avoid means the kings are kept out of the whisky's name

parts.note: Knockando is a Speyside single malt Scotch whisky
K is the chess abbreviation for king, so kings are two Ks

explanation.surface: Monarchs are told to steer clear of spirits, and politely decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Knockando is a Scotch whisky distillery on Speyside; removing both Ks leaves the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial refusal meaning that something cannot be managed.

clue.text: No way approve ambassador's lines

parts.note: to like something is to approve of it
an ambassador is styled His or Her Excellency, HE

explanation.surface: An envoy's script is firmly rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Like hell is an emphatic exclamation of refusal, an idiom for certainly not.

clue.text: Drivers en masse entering the old country

indicators.note: entering means going inside the word the

parts.note: the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation of drivers

explanation.surface: A convoy of motorists crosses into an ancient land.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region of the Balkans, home of the Thracians.

clue.text: Manx cat's weird, probably gutted

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or weird

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Manx cat is strange, probably disembowelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpy is a Manx cat with no tail at all, the breed's classic form.

clue.text: Confinement, note, in a form of funeral

indicators.note: in means the note's letter is placed inside the funeral word

parts.note: interment, burial, is one form of funeral

explanation.surface: A notice of someone being shut away arrives at a burial.
explanation.definitionFit: Internment is the detention of people, often without trial, in wartime camps.

clue.text: Flirty girl in short little skirt wanting kiss

indicators.note: wanting here is desiring, so the kiss is added on the end
short means the skirt word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A flirtatious girl in a miniskirt is angling for a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a cheeky or flirtatious young woman.

clue.text: Put out message when denied opening in court

indicators.note: denied opening means the first letter of the message word is dropped

parts.note: a text is a phone message

explanation.surface: A message is ruled inadmissible in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Extinct can describe a fire or light that has been extinguished, quenched like a volcano gone dead.

clue.text: Basically misquote regularly selected hearsay

indicators.note: regularly selected means letters are picked at a fixed interval, here every third

explanation.surface: Someone essentially misquotes, passing on rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: Every third letter of 'Basically misquote' is taken, starting with the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A say-so is a bare assertion with nothing but someone's word behind it, like hearsay.
